input.quote: Customer commits to purchase at least USD 2,000,000 of Services in each of the next three years on a take-or-pay basis, without reduction or termination rights.
input.rationale: Section 9 grants termination only for material breach (9.1), insolvency (9.2), and Vendor security/service-level/legal/IP failures (9.3), with a force-majeure exit in 27.3; no provision lets Customer terminate for convenience, and Section 2.1 affirmatively denies termination rights across a three-year take-or-pay commitment. That is walk-away territory (no Customer convenience right in a multi-year term) and fails the fallback. Section 10.2 refunds only "prepaid recurring Fees covering the period after termination", which is neither expressly pro rata nor coextensive with prepaid Fees as defined, so the refund element is carried in the new clause. The cure is a numbered Section 9.4 giving us a 30-day convenience exit with a pro-rata refund of prepaid Fees and confirming Vendor has no convenience right during a committed term, plus a conforming edit to 2.1 that keeps the no-reduction restriction intact.

proposal.summary: Add numbered Section 9.4: Customer 30-day convenience termination with pro-rata refund of prepaid Fees; no Vendor convenience right; conform 2.1
proposal.comment: [Playbook] We added a numbered Section 9.4 giving us a 30-day convenience exit with a pro-rata refund of prepaid Fees and confirming Vendor has no convenience termination right during a committed term. We also conformed the take-or-pay commitment so it no longer denies that termination right, leaving the no-reduction restriction intact.

ops.text: 9.4 Customer may terminate this Agreement or any Order Form for convenience upon thirty days' prior written notice to Vendor, in which case Vendor shall refund, on a pro rata basis, all prepaid Fees for the period after the effective date of termination. Vendor may not terminate this Agreement or an Order Form for convenience during a committed term.

ops.newText: without reduction rights, subject to Section 9.4

mappings.element: Customer may terminate the Agreement or an Order Form for convenience.
Customer's convenience termination requires no more than 30 days' written notice.
Vendor refunds prepaid fees pro rata after Customer's convenience termination.
Vendor has no right to terminate for convenience during a committed term.
